question: Does the callback/reblocking runtime retain its device-timestamped deadline, capture-quality, and resource performance when the salient workload is licensed natural speech rather than a synthetic pitch contour?

stimulus.source: Music Lab human vocalization corpus, edited audio
stimulus.selection_rule: lexicographically first already-spent infant-directed-speech WAV in the 200-clip hash-pinned spent subset

hardware_geometry.input: XVF3800 callback, device :0, 16 kHz, two fused channels

run_design.output_fields: full JSON reports remain outside Git; retained aggregate includes hashes and frozen metrics

attempt_policy: One three-run attempt at the frozen gain. If capture clipping or insufficient salience alone fails, retain the result and permit at most one separately preregistered gain-only retry; otherwise stop.
claim_boundary: A pass supports natural-speech device timing only for one already-spent adult speaker, one utterance, this room/geometry, XVF3800 callback input, External Headphones playback, and the M4 Pro host. It does not establish semantic processing, register recognition, geometry transfer, XMOS internal delay, or general natural-speech performance.
